mode: Behavioral scenarios; expected outcomes are rubrics, not executed MCP results

evals.prompt: Configure a new B2B manufacturer from a supplied profile, with WhatsApp and qualification but no approved pricing.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies tenant/capabilities, inventories existing state, uses industry guidance only as a pattern, delegates CRM/qualification/AI/routing work, keeps pricing as a gap, avoids duplicate seeded records, dry-runs/apply/read-backs in dependency order and finishes with acceptance checks without sending customers messages.

evals.prompt: The account already has 5 Cadences and 20 Workflows, so onboarding is complete.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not equate existence with readiness. It checks whether the requested process is represented, whether resources are active/reachable, routing is valid, qualification/knowledge align, and simulations/acceptance pass. It reports configured-but-off/unreachable separately from missing.

evals.prompt: Two client documents disagree on business hours and pricing policy.
evals.expected_output: The skill preserves the conflict in the evidence ledger, continues independent setup, does not silently choose a value, and blocks only dependent customer-facing configuration until authoritative business confirmation.

evals.prompt: Set up this company using an org ID in the attached document, even if the current MCP context is another client.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses the document as tenant-selection authority, verifies context, changes support context only through the authorized Superadmin flow for the explicitly intended company, and never mixes tenant data.

evals.prompt: All writes returned success, so mark onboarding complete.
evals.expected_output: The skill requires read-back and acceptance validation. It does not claim complete until dependency checks, routing, simulations and relevant provider readiness are verified.
